rows.blurb: Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank is the second-largest bank in Abu Dhabi, majority-owned by the emirate's government through its investment vehicle, with a retail, corporate and Islamic banking franchise concentrated in the UAE.

rows.name: Al Rajhi Banking and Investment Corporation
rows.blurb: Al Rajhi Bank is the largest Islamic bank in the world by assets and the largest retail bank in Saudi Arabia, funded by a large base of retail deposits and lending mainly to Saudi households under Sharia-compliant structures.

rows.name: The Saudi National Bank
rows.blurb: Saudi National Bank is the largest bank in Saudi Arabia, formed from the merger of National Commercial Bank and Samba, with the Public Investment Fund as its largest shareholder, funded by Saudi deposits and lending to Saudi corporates, government projects and households.

rows.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
rows.blurb: JPMorgan Chase & Co. is the holding company of the largest US bank, spanning consumer and community banking, the corporate and investment bank, commercial banking and asset and wealth management.

rows.name: JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A.
rows.blurb: JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. is the main operating bank of JPMorgan Chase, the largest bank in the United States, serving consumers, businesses, corporates and institutions across the country and worldwide.

rows.name: Bank of America Corporation
rows.blurb: Bank of America Corporation is the holding company of the second-largest US bank, spanning consumer banking, wealth management under Merrill and a global corporate and investment bank.

rows.name: Bank of America, N.A.
rows.blurb: Bank of America, N.A. is the main deposit-taking bank of Bank of America Corporation, the second-largest US bank by assets, serving consumers, small businesses and corporates across the United States.

rows.name: Citigroup Inc.
rows.blurb: Citigroup is the holding company of the most international of the large US banks, with services, markets, banking, wealth and US personal banking as its main lines, and a multi-year restructuring behind it.

rows.name: Citibank, N.A.
rows.blurb: Citibank, N.A. is the main operating bank of Citigroup, with the broadest international network of any US bank, serving multinationals, institutions and consumers across around a hundred countries.

rows.name: Wells Fargo & Company
rows.blurb: Wells Fargo & Company is the holding company of one of the four largest US banks, with consumer banking and lending, commercial banking, corporate and investment banking and wealth management, and a long regulatory remediation behind it.

rows.name: Wells Fargo Bank, N.A.
rows.blurb: Wells Fargo Bank, N.A. is the main operating bank of Wells Fargo, one of the four largest US banks, with the largest branch network in the country, serving consumers, small businesses and corporates across the United States.

rows.name: The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc.
rows.blurb: The Goldman Sachs Group is the holding company of the leading US investment bank, earning from advisory, trading and asset and wealth management, with a smaller lending and deposit franchise than the universal banks.

rows.name: Goldman Sachs Bank USA
rows.blurb: Goldman Sachs Bank USA is the US deposit-taking bank of The Goldman Sachs Group, holding the firm's lending, derivatives and Marcus consumer deposits, funded by deposits and by the parent.

rows.name: Morgan Stanley
rows.blurb: Morgan Stanley is the holding company of a leading US investment bank whose earnings have shifted toward wealth and investment management alongside institutional securities, with a deposit franchise built on brokerage sweeps.

rows.name: Morgan Stanley Bank, N.A.
rows.blurb: Morgan Stanley Bank, N.A. is the main US deposit-taking bank of Morgan Stanley, holding the firm's lending to wealth management clients and corporates, funded largely by brokerage sweep deposits.

rows.name: The Bank of New York Mellon Corporation
rows.blurb: BNY is the holding company of the world's largest custodian bank, earning fees from safekeeping, settlement, asset servicing and investment management for institutions rather than from lending.

rows.name: The Bank of New York Mellon
rows.blurb: The Bank of New York Mellon is the main operating bank of BNY, the world's largest custodian, whose business is safekeeping, settlement and asset servicing for institutions rather than lending to households.

rows.name: State Street Corporation
rows.blurb: State Street Corporation is the holding company of one of the world's largest custodian banks, earning fees from safekeeping, fund administration and asset management under the State Street Global Advisors brand.

rows.name: State Street Bank and Trust Company
rows.blurb: State Street Bank and Trust Company is the operating bank of State Street, one of the world's largest custodians, whose business is safekeeping, fund administration and asset servicing for institutions rather than lending to households.

rows.name: Northern Trust Corporation
rows.blurb: Northern Trust Corporation is the holding company of a Chicago-based custodian and wealth manager, earning fees from asset servicing for institutions and from managing money for wealthy families and foundations.

rows.name: The Northern Trust Company
rows.blurb: The Northern Trust Company is the operating bank of Northern Trust, a Chicago-based custodian and wealth manager whose business is asset servicing for institutions and banking for wealthy families rather than mass-market lending.

rows.name: UBS Group AG
rows.blurb: UBS Group is Switzerland's only remaining global bank after absorbing Credit Suisse, the world's largest wealth manager, with Swiss retail and corporate banking, asset management and an investment bank, and a balance sheet far larger than the Swiss economy.

rows.name: BNP Paribas Fortis SA/NV

negative.title: One of the three agencies downgraded its long-term rating
One of the three agencies removed its long-term rating under negative outlook

rows.blurb: BNP Paribas Fortis is the largest bank in Belgium and the Belgian retail and commercial arm of BNP Paribas, funded by Belgian deposits and lending to households, companies and the public sector, with Turkish and Luxembourg subsidiaries.

rows.name: OP Corporate Bank plc
rows.blurb: OP Corporate Bank is the corporate and central banking entity of OP Financial Group, Finland's largest financial group, handling wholesale funding, corporate lending and markets for the cooperative member banks.

rows.name: Credit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank
rows.blurb: Credit Agricole CIB is the corporate and investment bank of the Credit Agricole group, funded in wholesale markets and by corporate deposits, active in structured finance, capital markets and international trade and transaction banking.

rows.name: Credit Industriel et Commercial

negative.title: One of the three agencies maintained its long-term rating under negative outlook
One of the three agencies placed its long-term rating under negative outlook

rows.blurb: CIC is a French retail and corporate bank, the main non-mutual subsidiary of Credit Mutuel Alliance Federale, with a regional branch network across France and a corporate and investment banking arm.

rows.name: Landwirtschaftliche Rentenbank
rows.blurb: Rentenbank is Germany's development bank for agriculture and rural areas, a federal institution carrying an explicit guarantee from the German state, which funds itself in the bond markets and lends through other banks to farms, food businesses and rural infrastructure.

rows.name: Norddeutsche Landesbank Girozentrale
rows.blurb: NORD/LB is the Landesbank of Lower Saxony and Saxony-Anhalt, owned by the two states and the regional savings banks, a corporate, energy and real-estate lender that was recapitalised after shipping losses and also acts as central bank for its savings banks.

rows.name: NRW.BANK

negative.title: One of the three agencies removed its long-term rating under negative outlook

rows.blurb: NRW.BANK is the development bank of North Rhine-Westphalia, wholly owned by the state and carrying its explicit guarantee, which funds itself in the bond markets and lends for housing, infrastructure, small business and municipal purposes across the state.

rows.name: BNG Bank N.V.
rows.blurb: BNG Bank is the Dutch public-sector bank, owned by the Dutch state, provinces and municipalities, which lends almost entirely to Dutch local authorities, housing associations and healthcare bodies and funds itself in the bond markets.

rows.name: Nederlandse Waterschapsbank N.V.
rows.blurb: NWB Bank is the Dutch water boards' bank, owned by the water authorities, the Dutch state and the provinces, which lends to Dutch public-sector bodies, housing associations and healthcare providers and funds itself in the bond markets.

rows.name: Lloyds Bank Corporate Markets plc
rows.blurb: Lloyds Bank Corporate Markets is the non-ring-fenced bank of Lloyds Banking Group, housing its markets business, its Crown Dependency banking and lending to larger corporates outside the ring-fence, funded by corporate deposits and wholesale markets.

rows.name: National Bank of Kuwait (International) plc
rows.blurb: NBK International is the London-based bank of National Bank of Kuwait, the largest bank in Kuwait, serving the parent's Gulf clients in Europe with private banking, trade finance and property lending, funded by deposits and the parent.

rows.name: Santander Financial Services plc
rows.blurb: Santander Financial Services plc is the Santander group's bank in Jersey and the Isle of Man, offering deposits and lending to Crown Dependency and international clients, funded by those deposits and the group.

rows.name: SMBC Bank International plc
rows.blurb: SMBC Bank International is the London-based bank of Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation, serving the Japanese group's corporate and institutional clients across Europe, the Middle East and Africa, funded by corporate deposits and the parent.
